messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 3-chloropyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

picks.reason: This untested phenylisoxazole provides a simple aromatic comparison against the strong ester-substituted A9 additive.
Testing the 4-phenyl positional isomer can reveal whether the phenylisoxazole ring connectivity supports the high-yielding L2/B3 system.
This 3-phenylisoxazole probes a distinct isomer while retaining the aromatic substituent present in A1 and A2.
The dibenzylamino substituent may provide a useful donor group that changes additive behavior relative to simple phenylisoxazoles.
This positional isomer of the dibenzylamino additive tests whether donor-group placement affects performance.
A6 gave 27.2% with L2/B1, so testing it with the best-observed B3 base directly checks whether the stronger base improves its result.
A8 gave only 10.9% with L2/B2, but the leading L2/B3 conditions make a base-matched test worthwhile.
This compact dimethylisoxazole tests whether small alkyl substituents can retain activity without A9's ester group.
The pyrrolyl-substituted isoxazole offers a distinct donor-rich additive structure under the best ligand/base pair.
A13 is a close ester-substituted isoxazole analogue of A9 and is a strong candidate for transferring A9's additive benefit.
This methyl/phenyl-substituted isoxazole tests a more hydrophobic analogue while retaining the preferred reaction conditions.
The ester-bearing methoxyisoxazole offers a close functionalized analogue that may combine useful coordination with A9-like substitution.
The difluorophenyl group tests whether a more electron-poor aromatic substituent improves additive performance.
This heteroaryl ester analogue tests whether a furyl substituent can preserve the promising ester-isoxazole behavior.
The thiophene analogue of A21 provides a closely related heteroaryl ester comparison under the leading conditions.
A12 already gave 39.6% with L2/B3, so testing B2 checks whether the additive remains effective with the second-best base.
This tests whether A12's strong result is robust to the weaker-performing B1 base.
A17 reached 31.9% with L2/B3, and this experiment tests whether B2 can improve or sustain that promising result.
This base comparison will show whether A17's moderate activity depends specifically on B3.
As a close analogue of top-performing A9, A13 merits a comparison with B2 to assess base sensitivity.
